steps.name: Formulate Research Question and Hypothesis
steps.description: Define the precise hypothesis: A CT‑derived radiomics signature can accurately predict high‑risk neuroblastoma status at diagnosis. Specify primary (e.g., AUC for high‑risk prediction) and secondary (e.g., prediction of event‑free survival) endpoints.

steps.name: Comprehensive Literature Review
steps.description: Search PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and radiomics repositories for prior work on neuroblastoma imaging, radiomics pipelines, and risk stratification. Summarize gaps, methodological standards (e.g., Image Biomarker Standardisation Initiative), and benchmark performance metrics.

steps.name: Study Design Selection
steps.description: Choose a multicenter, retrospective‑prospective cohort design. The retrospective arm will provide a training dataset (n≥200), while the prospective arm will serve for internal validation (n≥100) and an external validation cohort (n≥100) from independent institutions.

steps.name: Sample Size and Power Calculation
steps.description: Perform simulations based on anticipated AUC (e.g., 0.85) with α=0.05 and 80 % power to detect a minimum clinically relevant AUC of 0.75. Estimate required number of high‑risk and low‑risk cases (target 1:1 or reflect real‑world prevalence) and inflate for drop‑outs and missing data (~10 %).

steps.name: Ethics, Regulatory Approvals, and Data‑Sharing Agreements
steps.description: Prepare IRB/REC submissions for each participating site, including consent waivers for retrospective data and informed consent forms for prospective enrolment. Draft Data Use Agreements (DUAs) covering de‑identification, GDPR/HIPAA compliance, and secure transfer of imaging and clinical data.

steps.name: Site Selection and Investigator Training
steps.description: Identify 4‑6 pediatric oncology centers with high neuroblastoma volume and standardized CT protocols. Conduct webinars on imaging acquisition standards, DICOM handling, and radiomics workflow (segmentation, feature extraction, quality control). Distribute a detailed operations manual.

steps.name: Eligibility Criteria Definition
steps.description: Inclusion: patients ≥18 years with histologically confirmed neuroblastoma, baseline contrast‑enhanced abdominal CT performed before any systemic therapy, and available MYCN, INSS stage, and serum markers. Exclusion: prior chemotherapy/radiotherapy, CT artifacts precluding segmentation, or incomplete clinical follow‑up.

steps.name: Standardized CT Acquisition Protocol
steps.description: Specify scanner parameters (e.g., 120 kV, 150‑250 mA, slice thickness ≤1.25 mm, portal venous phase 70 s after contrast). Provide phantom‑based calibration guidelines to harmonize voxel size, reconstruction kernel, and noise across sites.

steps.name: Imaging Data Collection and Central Repository Setup
steps.description: Deploy a secure, cloud‑based repository (e.g., REDCap + XNAT) for DICOM upload. Apply automated de‑identification scripts. Record scanner model, acquisition parameters, and timing relative to diagnosis for each case.

steps.name: Tumor Segmentation
steps.description: Perform semi‑automated 3D segmentation of the primary tumor using validated software (e.g., ITK‑Snap, 3D Slicer) with consensus review by two pediatric radiologists. Store masks in NIfTI format. Capture inter‑observer Dice similarity coefficient for a subset (≥30 cases).

steps.name: Radiomics Feature Extraction
steps.description: Extract quantitative features following the Image Biomarker Standardisation Initiative (IBSI) using PyRadiomics. Include first‑order statistics, shape descriptors, texture matrices (GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, NGTDM), and wavelet‑filtered features. Apply voxel‑size resampling (1 mm³) and intensity normalization (z‑score) before extraction.

steps.name: Feature Reproducibility and Harmonization
steps.description: Assess intra‑ and inter‑scanner reliability via Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) on a test‑retest subset (n≥30). Use ComBat harmonization to correct for batch effects across centers while preserving biological variance.

steps.name: Clinical Data Integration
steps.description: Collect demographic (age, sex), biologic (MYCN amplification, chromosome 1p/11q status, serum ferritin, LDH), and staging data (INSS, INRG). Encode high‑risk status per current COG criteria (age ≥ 18 months, stage ≥ 4, MYCN amplified, etc.).

steps.name: Dataset Partitioning
steps.description: Randomly split the retrospective cohort into training (70 %) and internal validation (30 %). Reserve the prospective cohort for temporal validation and the external sites for independent validation. Ensure stratification by risk status.

steps.name: Feature Selection and Dimensionality Reduction
steps.description: Apply a multi‑step pipeline: (1) filter out features with ICC < 0.75; (2) remove highly correlated features (Spearman ρ > 0.9) using hierarchical clustering; (3) employ univariate logistic regression (p < 0.05) as a pre‑screen; (4) use penalized regression (Elastic Net) within cross‑validation to select the final predictive set.

steps.name: Model Development
steps.description: Build a predictive model for high‑risk status using logistic regression, random forests, and gradient boosting (XGBoost). Optimize hyperparameters via nested 5‑fold cross‑validation on the training set. Record calibration curves and Brier scores.

steps.name: Model Evaluation
steps.description: Assess discrimination (AUC‑ROC, AUC‑PR), calibration (Hosmer‑Lemeshow test, calibration slope), and clinical usefulness (Decision Curve Analysis) on internal and external validation sets. Compute sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV at clinically relevant thresholds.

steps.name: Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP)
steps.description: Pre‑specify statistical methods, handling of missing data (multiple imputation), adjustment for potential confounders, and subgroup analyses (age < 12 months vs. ≥ 12 months, MYCN status). Include plans for bootstrapped confidence intervals for performance metrics.

steps.name: External Validation and Generalizability Testing
steps.description: Apply the finalized radiomics signature (fixed coefficients) to the external cohort without retraining. Evaluate performance drop‑off and conduct re‑calibration if needed. Perform sensitivity analysis excluding cases with non‑standard CT protocols.

steps.name: Exploratory Prognostic Analyses
steps.description: Correlate the radiomics risk score with event‑free survival and overall survival using Cox proportional hazards models, adjusting for known clinical risk factors. Test for interaction between radiomics score and MYCN status.

steps.name: Clinical Implementation Feasibility Study
steps.description: Prototype a cloud‑based decision support tool that inputs DICOM, runs the automated segmentation‑extraction‑prediction pipeline, and returns a risk probability within 5 minutes. Conduct a pilot usability test with pediatric oncologists and radiologists.

steps.name: Data Management, Quality Assurance, and Monitoring
steps.description: Establish a central data coordinating center. Use REDCap for clinical data, XNAT for imaging, and version‑controlled Git repositories for analysis scripts. Perform periodic audits, monitor protocol adherence, and log any deviations.

steps.name: Manuscript Preparation and Reporting
steps.description: Draft manuscripts following TRIPOD (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis) and CLAIM (Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging) guidelines. Include detailed methods, code availability statements, and supplemental tables for all extracted features.

steps.name: Dissemination and Knowledge Translation
steps.description: Present findings at ISPN, SIOP, and RSNA meetings. Submit the radiomics pipeline as an open‑source package on GitHub with Docker images for reproducibility. Engage with stakeholder groups (parents, clinicians) to develop educational material on the test’s interpretation.

steps.name: Future Directions and Funding Applications
steps.description: Identify gaps (e.g., integration with MRI‑based radiomics, longitudinal monitoring). Prepare grant proposals to expand the model to a multicenter prospective trial evaluating impact on treatment decision‑making and patient outcomes.

current_hypothesis.title: CT Radiomics Signature Predicts High‑Risk Neuroblastoma
current_hypothesis.intervention: Assessment of a radiomics‑derived imaging signature from CT imaging
current_hypothesis.outcome: Accurate prediction of high‑risk disease status
